message.content:
Columbia University is an Ivy‑League private research university located in Morningside Heights, Manhattan, New York City. Founded in 1754 as King's College by royal charter from King George II, it was renamed Columbia College in 1784 after the American Revolution and later became Columbia University in 1896 when it expanded into a full university. Key facts: | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Founded** | 1754 (as King's College) | | **Location** | Morningside Heights, Manhattan, NYC | | **Campus size** | ~36 acres (urban) | | **Student body** | ~33,000 total; ~8,500 undergraduates, ~24,500 graduate & professional students | | **Academic structure** | 16 schools & colleges (e.g., Columbia College, Fu Foundation School of Engineering & Applied Science, Mailman School of Public Health, Columbia Law School, Columbia Business School, Graduate School of Arts & Sciences) | | **Research focus** | Broad interdisciplinary research across humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, engineering, medicine, journalism, law, business, public health, etc. | | **Notable achievements** | • Nobel laureates: 38 (including 12 in Physics, 9 in Chemistry, 5 in Medicine, 2 in Economics, 1 in Peace).
• Pulitzer Prizes: 86 (most awarded institution).
• Nobel Prize winners among faculty/alumni include 10 physicists, 7 chemists, 4 economists, 3 physicians, 1 peace laureate.
• Major research centers: Columbia Genome Center, Columbia Data Science Institute, Columbia Climate Change Initiative. | | **Notable alumni** | • Presidents: Theodore Roosevelt, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Barack Obama (attended but did not graduate), William Howard Taft.
• Writers: Toni Morrison, James Baldwin, Langston Hughes.
• Scientists: Alexander Fleming (PhD), Jonas Salk (MD), Robert Gallo (MD).
• Entrepreneurs: Mark Zuckerberg (attended but dropped out). | | **Rankings** | Consistently ranked in top 20 U.S. universities by U.S. News & World Report, QS World University Rankings, Times Higher Education. | Columbia’s main campus sits on a hill overlooking Washington Square Park, with iconic buildings like Low Memorial Library, Butler Library, and the historic Hamilton Hall. It also operates several satellite campuses: Columbia University Medical Center (New York-Presbyterian Hospital), Columbia University Irving Medical Center, and the Columbia University School of Nursing at New York Hospital.
